message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: ci

on:
- pull_request
- push

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    permissions:
      checks: write  # for coverallsapp/github-action to create new checks
      contents: read  # for actions/checkout to fetch code
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      matrix:
        name:
        - Node.js 0.10
        - Node.js 0.12
        - io.js 1.x
        - io.js 2.x
        - io.js 3.x
        - Node.js 4.x
        - Node.js 5.x
        - Node.js 6.x
        - Node.js 7.x
        - Node.js 8.x
        - Node.js 9.x
        - Node.js 10.x
        - Node.js 11.x
        - Node.js 12.x
        - Node.js 13.x
        - Node.js 14.x
        - Node.js 15.x
        - Node.js 16.x
        - Node.js 17.x
        - Node.js 18.x
        - Node.js 19.x
        - Node.js 20.x
        - Node.js 21.x

        include:
        - name: Node.js 0.10
          node-version: "0.10"
          npm-i: mocha@3.5.3 nyc@10.3.2 supertest@2.0.0

        - name: Node.js 0.12
          node-version: "0.12"
          npm-i: mocha@3.5.3 nyc@10.3.2 supertest@2.0.0

        - name: io.js 1.x
          node-version: "1.8"
          npm-i: mocha@3.5.3 nyc@10.3.2 supertest@2.0.0

        - name: io.js 2.x
          node-version: "2.5"
          npm-i: mocha@3.5.3 nyc@10.3.2 supertest@2.0.0

        - name: io.js 3.x
          node-version: "3.3"
          npm-i: mocha@3.5.3 nyc@10.3.2 supertest@2.0.0

        - name: Node.js 4.x
          node-version: "4.9"
          npm-i: mocha@5.2.0 nyc@11.9.0 supertest@3.4.2

        - name: Node.js 5.x
          node-version: "5.12"
          npm-i: mocha@5.2.0 nyc@11.9.0 supertest@3.4.2

        - name: Node.js 6.x
          node-version: "6.17"
          npm-i: mocha@6.2.2 nyc@14.1.1 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 7.x
          node-version: "7.10"
          npm-i: mocha@6.2.2 nyc@14.1.1 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 8.x
          node-version: "8.17"
          npm-i: mocha@7.2.0 nyc@14.1.1 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 9.x
          node-version: "9.11"
          npm-i: mocha@7.2.0 nyc@14.1.1 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 10.x
          node-version: "10.24"
          npm-i: mocha@8.4.0 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 11.x
          node-version: "11.15"
          npm-i: mocha@8.4.0 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 12.x
          node-version: "12.22"
          npm-i: mocha@9.2.2 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 13.x
          node-version: "13.14"
          npm-i: mocha@9.2.2 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 14.x
          node-version: "14.21"
          npm-i: mocha@9.2.2 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 15.x
          node-version: "15.14"
          npm-i: mocha@9.2.2 supertest@6.1.6

        - name: Node.js 16.x
          node-version: "16.20"

        - name: Node.js 17.x
          node-version: "17.9"

        - name: Node.js 18.x
          node-version: "18.19"

        - name: Node.js 19.x
          node-version: "19.9"

        - name: Node.js 20.x
          node-version: "20.11"

        - name: Node.js 21.x
          node-version: "21.6"

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0

    - name: Install Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      shell: bash -eo pipefail -l {0}
      run: |
        nvm install --default ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        dirname "$(nvm which ${{ matrix.node-version }})" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

    - name: Configure npm
      run: |
        if [[ "$(npm config get package-lock)" == "true" ]]; then
          npm config set package-lock false
        else
          npm config set shrinkwrap false
        fi

    - name: Remove npm module(s) ${{ matrix.npm-rm }}
      run: npm rm --silent --save-dev ${{ matrix.npm-rm }}
      if: matrix.npm-rm != ''

    - name: Install npm module(s) ${{ matrix.npm-i }}
      run: npm install --save-dev ${{ matrix.npm-i }}
      if: matrix.npm-i != ''

    - name: Setup Node.js version-specific dependencies
      shell: bash
      run: |
        # eslint for linting
        # - remove on Node.js < 12
        if [[ "$(cut -d. -f1 <<< "${{ matrix.node-version }}")" -lt 12 ]]; then
          node -pe 'Object.keys(require("./package").devDependencies).join("\n")' | \
            grep -E '^eslint(-|$)' | \
            sort -r | \
            xargs -n1 npm rm --silent --save-dev
        fi

    - name: Install Node.js dependencies
      run: npm install

    - name: List environment
      id: list_env
      shell: bash
      run: |
        echo "node@$(node -v)"
        echo "npm@$(npm -v)"
        npm -s ls ||:
        (npm -s ls --depth=0 ||:) | awk -F'[ @]' 'NR>1 && $2 { print $2 "=" $3 }' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Run tests
      shell: bash
      run: |
        if npm -ps ls nyc | grep -q nyc; then
          npm run test-ci
        else
          npm test
        fi

    - name: Lint code
      if: steps.list_env.outputs.eslint != ''
      run: npm run lint

    - name: Collect code coverage
      uses: coverallsapp/github-action@09b709cf6a16e30b0808ba050c7a6e8a5ef13f8d # master
      if: steps.list_env.outputs.nyc != ''
      with:
        github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        flag-name: run-${{ matrix.test_number }}
        parallel: true

  coverage:
    permissions:
      checks: write  # for coverallsapp/github-action to create new checks
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: Upload code coverage
      uses: coverallsapp/github-action@09b709cf6a16e30b0808ba050c7a6e8a5ef13f8d # master
      with:
        github-token: ${{ secrets.github_token }}
        parallel-finished: true
",
  "rationale": "Two evidence-supported optimizations applied:
1. Added `timeout-minutes: 10` to the matrix `test` job (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). Experimental evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) shows a 26.8% elapsed-time reduction on a similar Node.js checkout/setup/install/lint workflow by bounding job runtime. The matrix tests 22 Node versions including legacy releases (0.10, io.js) that may install slowly or hang; a 10-minute budget provides operational headroom while capping runaway consumption.
2. Added workflow-level `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE). The pattern's simulation estimates a 4.1% paid VM time reduction by canceling superseded runs on the same branch/PR. This preserves required checks (each revision still runs to completion unless a newer push arrives) and partitions cancellation by workflow and ref as recommended.
Both changes are minimal, preserve all test coverage and required checks, and introduce no new permissions, secrets, or network access.",
  "evidence_ids": [
    "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508",
    "pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"
  ]
}

The user wants me to propose a CI optimization for the given workflow based on the evidence provided. I need to analyze the workflow and the evidence to see which optimization patterns are applicable.

First, let me understand the workflow:
- It's a CI workflow that runs on pull_request and push
- It has a matrix of Node.js versions from 0.10 to 21.x (22 versions)
- Each matrix job runs tests, linting, and collects coverage
- There's a coverage job that runs after all test jobs complete

The evidence includes several patterns from literature. Let me check which ones are applicable:

1. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** - There's experimental evidence showing 26.8% elapsed time savings by adding a 5-minute timeout. The workflow currently has no timeout. The matrix jobs test many Node versions, some very old (0.10, 0.12, io.js). These could potentially hang or take a long time. The evidence shows a measured case with similar structure (checkout, setup-node, install, lint, typecheck) where a 5-minute timeout saved time.

2. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** - Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure. The workflow has a large matrix (22 versions). If one fails, we could cancel the rest. However, the contraindication says "Every matrix outcome is required" - for a library testing compatibility across Node versions, all outcomes might be required. But the pattern says "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy". This might not apply if all versions are required.

3. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** - Cancel superseded runs. The workflow runs on push and PR. If multiple pushes to same branch/PR, we could cancel older runs. This seems applicable.

4. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** - Cache dependency downloads. The workflow uses `npm install` and installs various packages per matrix. There's no explicit caching. The pattern shows modest benefit (3.4% paid VM time reduction). The workflow uses `npm install` without cache. However, the setup-node action has `cache: npm` in the evidence example, but this workflow uses nvm directly, not setup-node.

5. **P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW** - Skip explicitly dispensable runs. Limited impact (0.1%). Contraindication: "Strict contract requires all triggers to execute". Might not apply.

6. **P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER** - Filter by changed paths. Limited impact (0.1%). The workflow tests a cookie-session middleware - changes likely affect all tests.

7. **P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST** - Run previously failing jobs first. Requires CI service support, not just workflow YAML.

8. **P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT** - Derive timeout from history. Similar to custom timeout but data-driven.

Looking at the experimental evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: it shows a 26.8% reduction in elapsed time by adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job. The workflow in evidence is similar: checkout, setup-node, npm ci, lint, typecheck, etc. Our workflow has a matrix with many Node versions, some very old that might be slow or hang. Adding a timeout could prevent runaway jobs.

The workflow currently has no timeout at job level. The default GitHub Actions timeout is 6 hours, which is excessive. Adding a reasonable timeout (e.g., 10-15 minutes per matrix job) could save resources if a job hangs.

Also, the workflow uses `nvm install` for each version, which can be slow for older versions. A timeout would bound this.

Let me check preconditions for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have one successful run in history (31012893673) that took about 56 seconds (from 13:59:22 to 14:00:18). But that's just one run. However, the pattern's experimental evidence shows it worked on a similar workflow.

The evidence IDs available: 
- experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)
- pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (the pattern itself)
- pattern:P-LIT-FAIL-FAST
- pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE
- pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE
- etc.

I need to choose APPLY with at least one evidence ID. The experimental evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) directly shows a measured improvement for a similar workflow by adding timeout-minutes: 5. That's strong evidence.

But wait: the experimental evidence shows a workflow with a single job (not matrix). Our workflow has a matrix of 22 jobs. Adding timeout to the matrix job would apply to each matrix instance. That seems reasonable.

Also, the workflow has a `coverage` job that depends on `test` job. The timeout should be on the `test` job (the matrix job).

Let me also consider P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: cancel superseded runs. This is a workflow-level setting (concurrency). The workflow doesn't have concurrency control. Adding `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` for PRs could cancel stale runs. The pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE has evidence (simulation estimate) showing 4.1% paid VM time reduction. Preconditions: "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR", "A newer revision supersedes older checks". This seems applicable for pull_request events.

But the instruction says "Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes." Adding concurrency control is a common optimization.

However, the experimental evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is more direct and measured (26.8% savings). The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is simulation estimate.

I think the best supported optimization is adding a custom timeout to the matrix job, based on the experimental evidence. Also, adding concurrency control for canceling stale runs is a good practice and supported by pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE.

But I need to choose one optimization? The instruction says "Propose any evidence-supported CI optimization". It doesn't say only one. But the output format expects a single workflow_yaml. I can include multiple changes in the updated workflow.

Let me check the evidence IDs: I can use multiple evidence_ids in the array.

I'll propose two changes:
1. Add `timeout-minutes: 10` to the `test` job (matrix job) - based on P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT experimental evidence.
2. Add `concurrency` to cancel stale runs for pull_request - based on P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern.

But wait: the workflow runs on both push and pull_request. For push events (to main branch), we might not want to cancel in-progress runs? Typically, concurrency with cancel-in-progress is used for PRs. We can set concurrency group per workflow and branch/PR.

The pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE says: "Partition cancellation by workflow and branch/PR". So we can add:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

This is a common pattern.

Now, for the timeout: what value? The experimental evidence used 5 minutes for a job that took median 34 seconds job runtime. Our test job matrix: the historical run took 56 seconds total for all matrix jobs? Actually, the run duration was 56 seconds for the whole workflow (including all matrix jobs running in parallel). Each matrix job likely takes less than a minute. But older Node versions might be slower. 10 minutes should be safe.

The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT says: "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom". 10 minutes gives plenty of headroom.

Let me also consider: the workflow uses `nvm install` which can take time for older versions. But 10 minutes should be enough.

Now, I need to produce the updated workflow YAML.

Let me write the updated workflow with both changes.

First, add concurrency at top level (after permissions?).

Second, add timeout-minutes to the test job.

Also, note that the workflow uses `actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0` - that's a specific SHA, good.

Now, the evidence IDs: I'll use:
- experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (for timeout)
- pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (for concurrency)

But the pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is a pattern document, not an experiment. The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one." The evidence IDs are the document_ids from the evidence array. I see document_id: "pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE" in the pattern catalogue. Also "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508" in the evidence array.

I'll include both.

Now, rationale: explain both changes.
